newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Email says strike may bite into sales soon.
newsitem.headline: Email says strike may bite into sales soon.

text.p: Australian industrial group Email Ltd said on Wednesday a five-week strike at one of its steel plants could start biting into sales soon.
But Email's group general manager of steel operations, Alan Freer, told Reuters the company's crippled Martin Bright Steel plant in Melbourne accounted for a fraction of total turnover.
Martin Bright Steel has been blockaded by picketing workers since April 11. It generates A$70 million of a total A$2.1 billion in group annual sales, Freer said.
He said customers dependent on the Martin Bright plant continued to operate by running down their own stocks.
"If people were to go back to work tomorrow we would anticipate we would recover most of the lost sales," Freer said.
"There's been enough stock in the value chain to have looked after most of our customers, but we are getting to that point where the value chain is using up all of that stock."
Asked if the strike had made an impact on profits, he said: "Not material at this stage."
Email and the Australian manufacturing Workers Union (AMWU), which is bargaining on behalf of Martin Bright Steel workers, are locked in a dispute over pay rises.
Workers on Tuesday rejected an offer of a 8.5 percent wage rise plus a two percent bonus over two years, the AMWU said.
Workers are holding out for at least 13 percent, AMWU organiser Craig Johnston told Reuters.
Freer called the AMWU's position unrealistic and said the company was seeking a court order declaring the union blockade of the plant illegal. This would allow picketers to be arrested.
Email is also trying to end the dispute by independent arbitration, he added.
"It's absolutely unrealistic to pay anybody 13 percent in this day and age in an internationally competitive industry," Freer said.
Thirty percent of Martin Bright Steel's products is exported to the United States, Asia and Europe, he said.
The AMWU has warned the dispute will escalate and spread if Email breaks up the picket forceably.
